summary: Behavior change: clear() (also the Clear button) while a request runs now stops that request; nothing of it is shown, stored or recorded, and the chat stays busy and empty until the transport reports the request's end. Before, the answer landed in the emptied chat.
howTo: Nothing to do with useVercelAiChatTransport or the LangGraph transport (the request ends at once). A custom ChatTransport is now stopped (stop(), best effort: a throw, a rejection or a missing stop() is caught) when the chat is cleared during a run; until its status leaves submitted/streaming the chat stays busy and empty, then the provider calls setMessages([]). A transport whose request does not end on stop() keeps the chat busy until it ends (no timeout). A message sent in that window goes out into the emptied chat afterwards: without the queue the first is held and submitWithResult reports { status: 'queued' }, a further one is { status: 'rejected', reason: 'session' }. Code that called clear() and then send() relied on two requests running at once; it now gets one fresh request. Tests that expected the answer after clear() stop relying on it. A host that switches session.activeId during the window shows that chat's own history; late writes of the cleared request into a shared transport can still land there (left-chat case). See docs/concepts.md, Turn outcomes.
